archetypes.name: migration-parity
archetypes.rationale: This diff replaces 12 bash scripts with python/voting.py; behavioral parity is the primary risk: vote thresholds, last-match-wins semantics, EXONERATE→NO mapping, PARSED_UNCERTAIN gating, no-trailing-newline contracts, and exit-code contracts (0/1/2) must match the originals exactly.
archetypes.prompt_body: Focus on verifying that python/voting.py faithfully replicates the behavioral contracts of the retired bash scripts. Check: (1) accept_finding and classify_result threshold matrices against eligible=0/1/2/3+ cases — particularly whether the eligible<=0 path returns 'rejected' not 'accepted' and whether the no-match path in parse_judge_vote correctly returns empty vote and empty axis fields at rc 0; (2) parse_judge_vote axis-before-delimiter parsing (scoped = scoped.split(' -- ', 1)[0] applied before axis tokenization) and PARSED_UNCERTAIN gating (true unless all three axes AND uncertain_token are present and valid, even when vote is empty due to invalid token); (3) split_ballot partial-write semantics: previously-written blocks may remain after a duplicate heading causes exit 1; (4) no-trailing-newline contract for reviewer_for_block_main, classify_result_main, and panel_tier_main (sys.stdout.write not print). Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: shell-cutover-safety
archetypes.rationale: Several shell scripts were updated to drop sourced bash libraries and call Python CLI instead; incomplete cutover, missing variable definitions under set -u, command-array scalar mix-ups, or stale source lines can cause runtime aborts or stdout contract violations in production runs.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect all updated shell consumer scripts for cutover correctness. Check: (1) every updated .sh file (dispatch-code-voters.sh, dispatch-plan-voters.sh, tally-code-votes.sh, tally-plan-review.sh, review-and-fix.sh, implement-bootstrap.sh, validate-research-output.sh, validate-citations.sh, oos-issue-cap.sh, oos-file-conflict-deps.sh) defines CLI, PLUGIN_ROOT/PY_CLI, DISPATCH_LABEL, and LAUNCH_MODE before first use under set -u; (2) write-tally invocation in review-and-fix.sh uses a command array (WRITE_TALLY_CMD=()) not a scalar, and retains 2>&1 capture around the command substitution so larch-log KV lines cannot leak to stdout; (3) no remaining source lines pointing to the 36 retired scripts; (4) parse-rate-retry call sites use command substitution where the Python process exits 0 even on NOT_SUBSTANTIVE, so set -e does not abort dispatch scripts; (5) effective-judges loop in dispatch-code-voters.sh still excludes skipped and failed slots without invoking Python retry for those slots. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: io-stream-routing
archetypes.rationale: The plan specifies precise stdout/stderr/fd-3/fd-4 contracts: parse-rate-retry prints a bare status token only, degraded-warning emits a single KV line to stdout, warning prose routes to fd-4 when LARCH_QUIET_ACTIVE is set, and quiet_init verbs must not contaminate plain stdout verbs.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify I/O stream routing contracts in python/voting.py. Check: (1) parse_rate_retry_main prints exactly the bare status token (OK or NOT_SUBSTANTIVE) to stdout with no PARSE_RATE_STATUS= prefix and no warning text mixed in — confirm the retry output read path strips or ignores any extra content before returning the bare token; (2) _plain_diagnostic routes to fd 4 via os.write(4, ...) when LARCH_QUIET_ACTIVE is truthy and LARCH_QUIET_PID is set, falling back to sys.stderr only when fd 4 is unavailable; (3) degraded_warning_main emits exactly one DEGRADED_PANEL_WARNING=... KV line to stdout and routes the banner prose through _plain_diagnostic, never to stdout; (4) reviewer_for_block_main, classify_result_main, and panel_tier_main use sys.stdout.write (no trailing newline) to match bash printf '%s' byte parity; (5) the three quiet_init verbs (parse_judge_vote_main, write_tally_main, compose_tally_record_main) call logging_util.quiet_init() and emit through emit_kv while all other verb mains use plain print. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
